title: Insider Trading Policy

tiers.name: Insiders
tiers.description: Employees, contractors, consultants and Board members, together with their immediate family members and anyone otherwise subject to their influence or control, and entities such as venture capital funds, partnerships, trusts and corporations associated or affiliated with them. Every substantive prohibition in the Policy (derivatives, hedging and monetisation, short selling, short-term trading, pledging as collateral) applies to this whole population; only blackout periods and pre-approval are confined to Section 16 Officers and Designated Insiders.

tiers.name: Section 16 Officers
tiers.description: The Company's executive officers and directors. Subject to all Insider restrictions plus Blackout Periods, pre-approval from the General Counsel and Chief Financial Officer before any trade, and a one business day post-trade notification to the General Counsel covering trades by them and their associates.

tiers.name: Designated Insiders
tiers.description: Individuals identified as having MNPI who are not Section 16 Officers but have regular access to MNPI in the normal course of their job: all Vice President level employees and above, administrative assistants to Section 16 Officers and Designated Insiders, legal function members preparing SEC filings and earnings materials, Investor Relations members assisting with earnings releases, Disclosure Committee members, designated Finance and Accounting members, and anyone else notified by the General Counsel and/or Chief Financial Officer. Subject to Blackout Periods and pre-approval but not to the one business day post-trade notification.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Immediate family members of Section 16 Officers and anyone otherwise subject to their influence or control (including household members), as well as entities such as venture capital funds, partnerships, trusts and corporations associated or affiliated with Section 16 Officers. 'Immediate family member' means any child, stepchild, parent, stepparent, spouse, domestic partner, sibling or in-law, and any person other than a tenant or employee sharing the household.

definitions.hedging_definition: Engage in hedging or monetization transactions involving our securities, such as zero cost collars and forward sale contracts, or contribute our securities to exchange funds in a manner that could be interpreted as hedging in our stock or otherwise limiting economic risk relating to the securities.

windows.end_anchor: the first trading day after the Company's Form 10-K has been released to ASX and filed with the SEC
the first trading day after the Company's Form 10-Q for the first quarter has been released to the ASX and filed with the SEC
the first trading day after the Company's Form 10-Q for the second quarter has been released to ASX and filed with the SEC
the first trading day after the Company's Form 10-Q for the third quarter has been released to ASX and filed with SEC

windows.start_anchor: any other period as the Board of the Company may decide

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The General Counsel and Chief Financial Officer may designate special trading Blackout Periods applying to specific individuals or groups, and the Board may decide any other period. Special Blackout Periods are strictly confidential: no one may tell anyone that a special Blackout Period has been designated or that one previously was in place, internally or externally.

rules.section: Prohibited Activities and Other Restrictions - Insider Restrictions
rules.detail: Flat ban on transactions in options or other derivative securities on Company stock, with puts and calls named and with express extension to off-exchange markets, so an OTC put and call written with a bank are squarely prohibited. The only carve-out is the exercise of equity awards issued by the Company. The ban applies to every Insider, not just Section 16 Officers and Designated Insiders, and there is no pre-approval route: only a Board waiver could permit it.
rules.evidence: Other than the exercise of equity awards issued by us, engage in transactions involving options or other derivative securities on our stock, such as puts and calls, whether on an exchange or in any other market.

rules.section: Prohibited Activities and Other Restrictions - Insider Restrictions
rules.detail: Hedging is prohibited outright with no distinction by vesting or restriction status and no approval route. Zero cost collars are named as an example, and the drafting reaches anything 'that could be interpreted as hedging in our stock or otherwise limiting economic risk relating to the securities', which captures a funded collar however documented.
rules.evidence: Engage in hedging or monetization transactions involving our securities, such as zero cost collars and forward sale contracts, or contribute our securities to exchange funds in a manner that could be interpreted as hedging in our stock or otherwise limiting economic risk relating to the securities.

rules.section: Prohibited Activities and Other Restrictions - Insider Restrictions
rules.detail: The hedging ban is not limited to plan or unvested securities. Vested, unrestricted shares and CDIs held outright are 'our securities' and hedging them is equally prohibited, which is the critical difference from most ASX policies that permit hedging of vested unrestricted holdings.
rules.evidence: Engage in hedging or monetization transactions involving our securities, such as zero cost collars and forward sale contracts

rules.section: Prohibited Activities and Other Restrictions - Insider Restrictions
rules.detail: Monetisation transactions are named and banned in the same breath as hedging, with forward sale contracts given as the example. A prepaid forward, a collar with a loan against the collared stock, or an exchange fund contribution are each prohibited.
rules.evidence: Engage in hedging or monetization transactions involving our securities, such as zero cost collars and forward sale contracts, or contribute our securities to exchange funds

rules.section: Prohibited Activities and Other Restrictions - Insider Restrictions
rules.detail: Absolute ban on short sales of Company securities, expressly including short sales 'against the box' (short positions taken while owning an equivalent long holding). This forecloses the argument that a covered downside position over shares actually held is acceptable.
rules.evidence: Engage in short sales of our securities, meaning a sale of securities that you do not own, including short sales "against the box."

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named and no definition sweeps it in. In practice a lend supporting a short position would engage the short sale ban, and a lend that transferred the securities as collateral would engage the pledging restriction.

rules.section: Prohibited Activities and Other Restrictions - Insider Restrictions
rules.detail: CFDs are not named. They are 'other derivative securities on our stock' traded in a market other than an exchange, so they fall within the express derivatives ban, and a short CFD would also breach the short sale ban and, if it limited economic risk of a holding, the hedging ban.
rules.evidence: engage in transactions involving options or other derivative securities on our stock, such as puts and calls, whether on an exchange or in any other market.

rules.section: Prohibited Activities and Other Restrictions - Insider Restrictions
rules.detail: Using or pledging Company securities as collateral in a margin account is prohibited unless the pledge has been approved by the General Counsel and complies with any applicable Company policy or guidelines regarding pledging. Margin lending is named as the example. The pledging guidelines are not part of this document.
rules.evidence: Use or pledge our securities as collateral in a margin account or as collateral for a loan (e.g. margin lending or similar funding arrangements) unless the pledge has been approved by our General Counsel and in accordance with any applicable policy or guidelines of the Company regarding pledging.

rules.section: Prohibited Activities and Other Restrictions - Insider Restrictions
rules.detail: Any pledge of Company securities as collateral, whether into a margin account or for a loan, requires General Counsel approval and compliance with the Company's pledging guidelines. Section 16 Officers and Designated Insiders would in addition need pre-approval for any associated transfer of securities.
rules.evidence: Use or pledge our securities as collateral in a margin account or as collateral for a loan ... unless the pledge has been approved by our General Counsel

rules.section: Prohibited Activities and Other Restrictions - Insider Restrictions
rules.detail: The restriction is drafted broadly to cover collateral 'for a loan (e.g. margin lending or similar funding arrangements)', so it is not confined to margin loans. A bank loan secured on Life360 shares or CDIs is therefore available in principle, but only with General Counsel approval and subject to unseen Company pledging guidelines. It cannot rescue the collar, whose derivative legs are separately banned.
rules.evidence: Use or pledge our securities as collateral in a margin account or as collateral for a loan (e.g. margin lending or similar funding arrangements) unless the pledge has been approved by our General Counsel

rules.section: Prohibited Activities and Other Restrictions - Insider Restrictions
rules.detail: Intention-based six month rule running in both directions: acquiring securities with a view to selling within six months, and selling with a view to repurchasing within six months, are both prohibited. Exercise of an option or sale of any grant under a Company equity incentive plan is carved out of the acquisition limb. Section 16 Officers are separately subject to the US short swing profit rules.
rules.evidence: Purchase of Life360 securities on the open market and trading the same on a short-term basis. For the purposes of this Policy, short-term trading includes acquiring securities (but not including the exercise of an option or sale of any grant under an equity incentive plan operated by the Company) with a view to selling the securities within a 6 month period as well as selling securities with a view to repurchase within a 6 month period.

clearance.approver: General Counsel and Chief Financial Officer; email confirmation comes from the General Counsel. Approval can be withdrawn or refused by the General Counsel, the Chief Financial Officer, the CEO or the Company in its discretion
clearance.post_trade_to: General Counsel (details of the trade including the number and price of the securities involved), for trades by the Section 16 Officer and their associates
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within one business day following a trade
clearance.section: Additional Restrictions Applicable to Section 16 Officers and Designated Insiders; Notification of trade
clearance.evidence: Prior to trading our securities, Section 16 Officers and Designated Insiders must also obtain pre-approval from our General Counsel and Chief Financial Officer by: (a) providing written notification of the amount and nature of the proposed trade ...; (b) certifying no earlier than two business days prior to the proposed trade that you have no MNPI; and (c) receiving email confirmation from our General Counsel approving the trade ... An approval to trade expires five business days from its date, unless the approval specifies a different date.

clearance.approver: General Counsel and Chief Financial Officer; email confirmation from the General Counsel, withdrawable by the General Counsel, Chief Financial Officer, CEO or the Company
clearance.section: Additional Restrictions Applicable to Section 16 Officers and Designated Insiders
clearance.evidence: Any approval to trade can be withdrawn or refused by the General Counsel, the Chief Financial Officer, the CEO or the Company in its discretion (and will be automatically deemed to have been withdrawn where the person seeking approval becomes aware of MNPI).

clearance.approver: General Counsel approval is nonetheless required for a pledge of securities as collateral, and for a gift, charitable contribution or other transfer of securities during a period when the Insider cannot otherwise trade
clearance.section: When Trading Is Allowed; Insider Restrictions
clearance.evidence: Insiders who are not Section 16 Officers or Designated Insiders and who are not in possession of MNPI may trade Company securities consistently with this Policy at any time.

short_term.basis: acquiring with a view to selling within 6 months, and selling with a view to repurchase within 6 months
carve_outs: the exercise of an option under an equity incentive plan operated by the Company
sale of any grant under an equity incentive plan operated by the Company
short_term.evidence: short-term trading includes acquiring securities (but not including the exercise of an option or sale of any grant under an equity incentive plan operated by the Company) with a view to selling the securities within a 6 month period as well as selling securities with a view to repurchase within a 6 month period.

exceptions.evidence: 401(k) Plan. Investing 401(k) plan contributions in a company stock fund in accordance with the terms of our 401(k) plan. However, any changes in your investment election regarding the Company's securities are subject to trading restrictions under this Policy.

Options. Exercising stock options granted under our equity incentive plans for cash or by delivering to the Company previously owned Company stock or through a net exercise of a stock option ... that does not involve a sale of shares in the open market.

RSUs. Disposition of RSUs pursuant to a net settlement or a "sale to cover" for non-discretionary, automatic tax withholdings initiated and pre-approved by the Company for the payment of taxes upon the vesting of RSUs.

exceptions.approver: General Counsel and Chief Financial Officer, for Section 16 Officers and Designated Insiders
exceptions.evidence: Estate Planning. Transfers of securities in connection with bona fide estate planning purposes, such as a transfer to or from a family trust or partnership. However, Section 16 Officers and Designated Insiders must get pre-approval from the General Counsel and Chief Financial Officer to transfer any Company securities.

Our Board reserves the right in its sole discretion to modify or grant waivers to this Policy. Any amendments or waiver may be publicly disclosed if required by applicable laws, rules and regulations.

financing.price_trigger_guidance: No trigger guidance in the Policy itself. Any pledge must be 'in accordance with any applicable policy or guidelines of the Company regarding pledging', a separate document that is not attached and that may contain loan-to-value or trigger constraints.
financing_disclosure: All Insiders: at inception, the pledge of Company securities as collateral in a margin account or for a loan requires the approval of the General Counsel; no deadline or form stated.

Section 16 Officers: within one business day following a trade, they and their associates must notify the General Counsel of the details of the trade including the number and price of the securities involved.
Section 16 Officers: separately subject to US beneficial ownership and short swing profit reporting under Section 16, and to Rule 144 resale limits, which the Policy notes but does not detail.

external_documents: Company policy or guidelines regarding pledging (referred to but not attached)
exemption_authority: The Board reserves the right in its sole discretion to modify or grant waivers to this Policy, and any waiver may be publicly disclosed if required by applicable laws, rules and regulations. Below that, the General Counsel administers and interprets the Policy, approves pledges of securities as collateral, and may approve gifts or transfers during a period when the Insider cannot otherwise trade; the General Counsel may delegate these duties. There is no hardship or exceptional-circumstances mechanism for trading during a Blackout Period.
jurisdiction_overlays: US federal securities laws: Section 16 short swing profit rules for executive officers and directors, and Section 16 reporting
Rule 144 under the US Securities Act of 1933 (resale limits)

Regulation S: the CDIs are 'restricted securities' under Rule 144 and bear a FOR Financial Product designation restricting sale on ASX to US persons other than QIBs; hedging transactions with regard to the CDIs may only be conducted in accordance with the Securities Act
US SEC filing regime (Forms 10-K and 10-Q drive the Blackout Period end dates alongside ASX release)
Australian Corporations Act insider trading provisions and ASX Listing Rules

bespoke_clauses.clause: Engage in hedging or monetization transactions involving our securities, such as zero cost collars and forward sale contracts, or contribute our securities to exchange funds in a manner that could be interpreted as hedging in our stock or otherwise limiting economic risk relating to the securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The precise structure a funded collar uses is named as a prohibited activity for every Insider, with no vesting carve-out and no clearance route, so the transaction cannot be done without a Board waiver.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Other than the exercise of equity awards issued by us, engage in transactions involving options or other derivative securities on our stock, such as puts and calls, whether on an exchange or in any other market.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Documenting the put and call bilaterally with a bank rather than on an exchange does not avoid the prohibition, which expressly reaches any other market.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Engage in short sales of our securities, meaning a sale of securities that you do not own, including short sales "against the box."
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a fully covered downside position against shares the executive already owns is caught, removing the usual argument that a collar over an existing holding is not a short sale.

bespoke_clauses.topic: pledging is the one permitted financing route
bespoke_clauses.clause: Use or pledge our securities as collateral in a margin account or as collateral for a loan (e.g. margin lending or similar funding arrangements) unless the pledge has been approved by our General Counsel and in accordance with any applicable policy or guidelines of the Company regarding pledging.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg alone is achievable with General Counsel approval, so a plain share-secured loan without any hedge is the only part of the funded collar that survives, subject to unseen pledging guidelines.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Our Board reserves the right in its sole discretion to modify or grant waivers to this Policy. Any amendments or waiver may be publicly disclosed if required by applicable laws, rules and regulations.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only route to a collar is an express Board waiver, which may have to be publicly disclosed under US rules, making it a high-visibility ask.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Our General Counsel and Chief Financial Officer may designate special trading Blackout Periods that apply to specific individuals or groups of people ... no one may tell anyone that a special Blackout Period has been designated or that one previously was in place because that also is confidential information that cannot be disclosed internally or externally.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An executive could be blocked from any permitted step, such as pledging or unwinding, without being able to explain the reason to the bank.

bespoke_clauses.clause: short-term trading includes acquiring securities ... with a view to selling the securities within a 6 month period as well as selling securities with a view to repurchase within a 6 month period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The look-forward period is six months rather than the usual three, so even the share transfers and repurchases around a financing would need a longer horizon.

bespoke_clauses.topic: Regulation S hedging restriction on CDIs
bespoke_clauses.clause: From the ASX announcement cover page: 'the CDIs are restricted securities under Rule 144 of the Securities Act ... In addition, hedging transactions with regard to the CDIs may only be conducted in accordance with the Securities Act.'
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even if the Policy were waived, US securities law independently constrains hedging of the CDIs, so the bank would need a Regulation S and Rule 144 analysis on top of the trading policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any approval to trade can be withdrawn or refused by the General Counsel, the Chief Financial Officer, the CEO or the Company in its discretion (and will be automatically deemed to have been withdrawn where the person seeking approval becomes aware of MNPI).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Approval is not a bankable condition precedent; it lapses automatically on the executive becoming aware of material nonpublic information before execution.

bespoke_clauses.topic: gifts and transfers in closed periods
bespoke_clauses.clause: Unless approved in advance by our General Counsel, make a gift, charitable contribution or other transfer of our securities during a period when the Insider cannot otherwise trade.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Delivering or transferring the collateral shares to a lender or custodian during a Blackout Period would itself require prior General Counsel approval.

summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy. The Insider Restrictions ban, for every Insider and with no vesting carve-out and no pre-clearance route, both transactions in options or other derivative securities on Company stock (puts and calls, expressly whether on an exchange or in any other market) and hedging or monetization transactions, with zero cost collars and forward sale contracts named as the paradigm examples and the drafting extending to anything that could be interpreted as limiting economic risk relating to the securities. Short sales, including short sales against the box, are separately banned, which forecloses the argument that a collar over shares actually held is merely covered risk management. Only the financing leg is achievable in isolation: pledging Company securities as collateral in a margin account or for a loan is permitted if the General Counsel approves and the Company's separate pledging guidelines are met, and Section 16 Officers and Designated Insiders would also need pre-approval from the General Counsel and Chief Financial Officer, execution within five business days, and to stay outside the January, April, July and October Blackout Periods, with a one business day post-trade notification for Section 16 Officers. The only route to the full structure is a Board waiver, which the Board may grant in its sole discretion but which may have to be publicly disclosed, and US Regulation S and Rule 144 constraints on hedging the CDIs would still have to be cleared separately.
